summary: Fixed null crmProfileId crash in disposition writers. In distribute/route.ts (lines 98-112) replaced `crmProfileId!` with a spread conditional that omits the disposition op entirely when crmProfileId is null, preventing the non-null assertion from throwing inside the transaction and rolling back the whole round-robin distribute. In redistribute/route.ts (lines 87-105) wrapped the audit insert in an `if (session.user.crmProfileId)` guard plus a try/catch that logs but does not rethrow, so both a null crmProfileId and any other audit insert failure leave the primary crmColdLead.update intact. Both changes tagged with `audit v12 HIGH` comment.

Applied boundedJson size cap to POST createSchema in src/app/api/saved-views/route.ts. Added a local `boundedJson` validator (mirrors the one in [id]/route.ts) that rejects any single field exceeding 8 KB serialised, and wired it to the `filters`, `sort`, and `columns` fields in `createSchema`. Also added a 32 KB total-body ceiling check in the POST handler — the request text is read via `req.text()` before parsing, and a 413 is returned if the raw length exceeds 32 768 bytes. Both changes are tagged with comment referencing audit v12 HIGH #36.

Fixed: The `crmAlertRuleFire.create` suppression row was written unconditionally after the channel-dispatch block, even when no notification was actually delivered (e.g. channels=['slack'] with no adapter, or targetUserId null). Introduced a `delivered` boolean flag set to `true` only inside the successful `in-app` branch; the `crmAlertRuleFire.create` call and `fired` increment are now guarded by `if (delivered)`. This ensures the suppression row is only recorded when a real notification went out, preventing entities from being silently and permanently skipped on subsequent cron ticks. Both changes are tagged with `// audit v12 HIGH` comments.

Fixed REP role-scope bypass in getCalls: the `repId` field has been removed from the `CallFilters` type and the code block that unconditionally wrote `where.callerId = filters.repId` (overriding the scope set by `scopeCallByRole`) has been eliminated. For REP role, `scopeCallByRole` returns `{ callerId: session.id }`; previously any caller could append `?repId=<other-rep>` to overwrite that scope and read another rep's full call history. The fix was applied via the edit to actions.ts (lines 131-163); the linter reformatted the file, confirming the final state: `CallFilters` no longer has a `repId` field, and no code path can override the role-scoped `callerId` filter. Applied PII mask to the per-id GET handler in the meetings [id] route. After fetching the full meeting record, non-scheduler non-manager callers (e.g. approvers) now have contactPhone, contactName, customerNeed, notes, and deniedReason nulled out before the response is sent — matching the exact mask already applied by the list endpoint. The `isManager` helper already present in the file is reused to grant full visibility to MANAGER/ADMIN/super_admin roles.

Applied audit v12 HIGH fix: added canAccessCompany check to block cross-company OT approvals, and added a team_lead subordinate-chain check using getSubordinateEmployeeIds so a team_lead can only approve OT for employees in their own report hierarchy. Also updated the permission gate from isHROrAdmin to can(authUser, 'overtime:approve') so that team_lead role is correctly admitted by the unified permission table.

Added cross-company authorization gate in the incident POST handler. After looking up the employee, a call to `canAccessCompany(authUser, employee.companyId)` now blocks HR managers from filing incidents against employees at companies they do not have access to, returning HTTP 403. Also added `canAccessCompany` to the import from `@/lib/hr/permissions`. The audit v12 HIGH comment tags the new guard. The single TSC error reported (`src/app/api/cron/alert-rules/route.ts:5`) is pre-existing and unrelated to this change.

Added company-scope filter for non-super_admin users who have canViewAllEmployees permission (accountant, ceo, hr_manager). Previously, when canViewAllEmployees returned true, no companyId restriction was applied, allowing cross-tenant leakage of employee records including salary, nationalId, and IBAN. The fix adds an else-if branch: when the user has view-all permission but is NOT super_admin, where.companyId is scoped to { in: authUser.companies } (unless the caller already narrowed to a specific company via the query param). Also added isSuperAdmin to the permissions import.

Fixed the silent account-hijacking vulnerability in the employee create endpoint. When a `work_email` matching an existing User account was supplied, the code now returns HTTP 409 with a descriptive error message and rolls back the already-created HrEmployee row, instead of silently binding the existing account (which would flip `hrAccess=true` and reassign `HrEmployee.userId` to the existing user without consent). The guard was inserted at line 195 of the file, tagged with `audit v12 HIGH`, before the `if (!existingUser)` branch that creates a fresh linked account.

Tightened offenseSchema.deduction_pct in incident.ts to enforce min(0) and max(100) for both number and string union branches, preventing hr_manager from saving negative or >100% deduction percentages. Tagged with audit v12 HIGH comment. The route.ts file already uses createViolationRuleSchema via safeParse so it benefits automatically. One pre-existing unrelated TSC error exists in src/app/api/cron/alert-rules/route.ts (evalPredicate not exported from CRM engine) — not introduced by this change.

Fixed PATCH cross-company gate in the HR bonuses route. The handler now fetches the existing bonus record and validates that the authenticated user can access its current company before processing any update. When `data.employee` is supplied (bonus reassignment), it additionally looks up the target employee and calls `canAccessCompany(authUser, targetEmployee.companyId)`, returning 403 if the caller does not have access to the target employee's company. The `employeeId` field is now only written after both checks pass. `canAccessCompany` was added to the import from `@/lib/hr/permissions`. Both guard blocks are tagged with `// audit v12 HIGH` comments.

Added a status guard in the PATCH handler (lines 85-113) that fetches the current leave request status before applying any field updates. If the request is already 'approved' or 'denied' and the PATCH body includes any of start_date, end_date, leave_type, or days_count, the handler now returns HTTP 409 with a clear message instructing the caller to revoke and re-create. This prevents the orphaned-attendance-log scenario where approved leave days (e.g. 20-24) would retain their 'leave' status while the newly patched range (e.g. 27-31) has no 'leave' rows at all. Status-only and reason-only edits on finalised requests are still allowed. The pre-existing TypeScript error in src/app/api/cron/alert-rules/route.ts (unrelated module export issue) was already present before this change; no errors

Replaced the plain `prisma.hrLeaveRequest.update` in the deny route with `updateMany({ where: { id: pk, status: 'pending' }, ... })`. When two concurrent deny requests race through the read-check together, only the first will match the `status: 'pending'` predicate and get count=1; the second gets count=0 and receives a 409, preventing the double-fire of the "Leave Request Denied" notification. The change is tagged with an `// audit v12 HIGH` comment at lines 35-36 of the modified file.

Added cross-company authorization gate to both the leave-approve and leave-deny routes. After the leave request is fetched from the database, a call to `canAccessCompany(authUser, lr.employee.companyId)` now guards both handlers. An HR manager whose companies list does not include the employee's company receives a 403 before any status mutation or attendance log write can occur. The import of `canAccessCompany` was added to both files. Changes are tagged with `// audit v12 HIGH` comments.
Distribute response reports `assigned: parsed.data.leadIds.length` even when terminal-state filter dropped some — toast lies to the manager
Orphan-stage opps render in a 'sortable' column the server then approves every transition for, because canTransition fails-open on unknown source codes.
Mention picker entity scope uses CALLER's entity, but the POST handler validates against the OPP's entity — picker can suggest users the server will silently drop
When the caller has no crmEntityId (null), the picker returns only users with null entityId plus mgrs/admins — non-mgr/admin users with no entity see an empty roster
POST stores body containing arbitrary @<cuid-shaped> tokens with no scrubbing — caller can plant a cross-entity profile id and have it broadcast in the thread (paired with the renderer fallthrough)
DELETE moderation check allows any CRM MANAGER (org-wide scope) to delete comments on any opp — even on opps whose entity they don't 'own' in the business sense
POST silently degrades SPECIFIC-with-no-targets to OWNER while PATCH returns 422 — inconsistent error contract for the same logical input.
PATCH silently ignores sharedWithIds when visibility moves to EVERYONE/OWNER — no warning that the list was discarded.
Self-exclusion in SpecificPeoplePicker depends on useSession() being ready — initial render of the picker briefly shows the owner in their own roster until the session hook resolves.
Roster fetch failure toast surfaces — but the picker still gets stuck rendering 'Loading users…' indefinitely; there's no retry button or visible empty-state for the failure path.
setMonth-based reset window has month-rollover bug at end-of-month incident dates — window can be 1-3 days SHORTER, dropping legitimate prior offenses.
Single-row OT approve has no cross-company gate even though the v11-fixed bulk-approve does — team_lead can approve OT for a foreign employee.
Dead `conflictingClient` query — soft-client cross-partner conflict check was removed but the read still runs, costing a SELECT on every registration POST
Non-WON 'normal update' branch on a PENDING deal lets partner edit `value` and `notes` without recomputing future commission
Target-active TOCTOU — impersonation row is created against a target that was deactivated between the active-check and the transaction
Non-HR-linked admin reset-password creates a stub HrUserProfile with isActive=false outside the transaction — leaves orphan stubs if the transaction fails
Audit-log unified GET filter params (entity / userId / action / startDate / endDate / page) have no Zod / length bound and invalid startDate is passed into new Date() unchecked
Cold-leads export GET filter params (industry, category, location, q, assignedToId, status) are unbounded — opposite of the bounded list GET in route.ts:53-57
load() and save() in admin pipelines client still silent — only toggleActive() got the v11 toast fix.

widgetSchema's `params` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).optional()` — unbounded other than the 16 KB JSON.stringify cap. An owner can stuff `params` with up to ~15.9 KB of arbitrary data per dashboard.
Dashboard error banner uses a tautological count formula and Arabic locale never sees the real count.
Active-target check counts an unset partner profile as 'active', so a deactivated partners-admin user can still be impersonated
Distribute response reports parsed.data.leadIds.length as 'assigned', overcounting when CONVERTED/ARCHIVED leads were silently filtered out
Dashboard failed-widgets banner message hardcodes a denominator of 6 but only 5 queries exist for non-super-admin (payrollSummaryQuery is disabled).
